newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Berjaya Group sells unit stake to Maju.
newsitem.headline: Berjaya Group sells unit stake to Maju.

text.p: Berjaya Group Bhd said on Thursday that it is selling a 79.95 percent stake in its Berjaya Singer Bhd unit to steel concern Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd for 1.20 billion ringgit.

In a statement, Berjaya Group said the sale price is 5.30 ringgit per share. As part of the proposed sale, Berjaya Group has extended a letter of offer to Berjaya Singer to buy back all existing units of the appliance maker via Tegas Kinta Sdn Bhd for a total of 1.32 billion ringgit in cash.
Shares of the Berjaya companies were suspended earlier on Thursday pending announcements.
The stake purchase of Berjaya Singer by Maju had been anticipated. Last week, an industry source close to the deal confirmed the deal was being done.

Maju is leading the rescue of loss-making, state-controlled Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd. Analysts had speculated Maju could be acquiring Berjaya Singer in order to use it as a shell company to inject Perwaja's assets.

Malaysia's government said earlier this year that it was assuming nearly 2.9 billion ringgit ($1.16 billion) in losses racked up by Perwaja, which is being probed by anti-corruption officials for alleged irregularities.

Berjaya Singer said in a separate statement that the proposals "will enable Berjaya Singer to participate as a major stakeholder in the privatisation of the restructured Perwaja which is to be funded from the internal cash resources".

Upon completion of the proposals, the total gross gain accruing to Berjaya Group would be 439.39 million ringgit, said Berjaya Group. The company said it expects to realise a gain of about 115.85 million ringgit from the deal.
Maju had said on Tuesday it had entered into a pact with steel firm Perwaja Terengganu Sdn Bhd to buy from Perwaja a 51 percent stake in Equal Concept Sdn Bhd for 1.02 billion ringgit.
Equal Concept has been managing Perwaja while its privatisation plan is being worked out.
